blocks.text: Even when those processes occur, there is no loss or disruption, because of the condition of being the conscious knower.
blocks.directed: Even when those processes occur, there is no loss or disruption, because of the condition of being the conscious knower.

blocks.text: The Universe Can Disappear. You Haven’t.
blocks.directed: The Universe Can Disappear. You Haven’t.

blocks.text: Now this is one of the deepest metaphysical statements in the entire text.
blocks.directed: Now this is one of the deepest metaphysical statements in the entire text.

blocks.text: And we need to take it seriously.
blocks.directed: And we need to take it seriously.

blocks.text: Because Kṣemarāja explicitly raises the objection.
blocks.directed: Because Kṣemarāja explicitly raises the objection.

blocks.text: Manifestation, maintenance and dissolution seem to be different states.
blocks.directed: Manifestation, maintenance and dissolution seem to be different states.

blocks.text: So if the yogi’s conscious nature is associated with all three, mustn’t that nature undergo corresponding changes?
blocks.directed: So if the yogi’s conscious nature is associated with all three, mustn’t that nature undergo corresponding changes?

blocks.text: Tat — those; referring to the preceding cosmic operations.
blocks.directed: Tat — those; referring to the preceding cosmic operations.

blocks.text: Anirāsaḥ — no disappearance, rejection, disruption or loss.
blocks.directed: Anirāsaḥ — no disappearance, rejection, disruption or loss.

blocks.text: Bhāvāt — because of the condition or nature of.
blocks.directed: Bhāvāt — because of the condition or nature of.

blocks.text: Even when the processes of manifestation and withdrawal occur, the realised yogi’s fundamental conscious nature is not lost.
blocks.directed: Even when the processes of manifestation and withdrawal occur, the realised yogi’s fundamental conscious nature is not lost.

blocks.text: Because it is the reality of the knower.
blocks.directed: Because it is the reality of the knower.

blocks.text: Changes in what is known do not entail the disappearance of the knowing principle.
blocks.directed: Changes in what is known do not entail the disappearance of the knowing principle.

blocks.text: But the fact that one scene ends does not mean the actor’s fundamental capacity to perform has ceased.
blocks.directed: But the fact that one scene ends does not mean the actor’s fundamental capacity to perform has ceased.

blocks.text: Now, with Śiva we have to go further.
blocks.directed: Now, with Śiva we have to go further.

blocks.text: Because the conscious knower isn’t a finite actor standing outside the universe.
blocks.directed: Because the conscious knower isn’t a finite actor standing outside the universe.

blocks.text: It is the luminous reality through which all these manifestations become possible.
blocks.directed: It is the luminous reality through which all these manifestations become possible.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja describes that reality through:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And Kṣemarāja describes that reality through:

blocks.text: These are not three independent substances.
blocks.directed: These are not three independent substances.

blocks.text: They describe the self-revealing nature of consciousness in the tradition’s terminology.
blocks.directed: They describe the self-revealing nature of consciousness in the tradition’s terminology.

blocks.text: And the crucial point is that consciousness does not cease when a particular differentiated object disappears.
blocks.directed: And the crucial point is that consciousness does not cease when a particular differentiated object disappears.

blocks.text: Now Kṣemarāja brings in the Spandakārikā.
blocks.directed: Now Kṣemarāja brings in the Spandakārikā.

blocks.text: And this is where the explanation becomes exceptionally beautiful.
blocks.directed: And this is where the explanation becomes exceptionally beautiful.

blocks.text: Kāryatā — the condition of being an effect or product.
blocks.directed: Kāryatā — the condition of being an effect or product.

blocks.text: The realm of manifest products is perishable.
blocks.directed: The realm of manifest products is perishable.

blocks.text: The deeper power of agency is not understood as perishing in the same way.
blocks.directed: The deeper power of agency is not understood as perishing in the same way.

blocks.text: We’re not simply saying your personal ability to do things remains unchanged forever.
blocks.directed: We’re not simply saying your personal ability to do things remains unchanged forever.

blocks.text: The kartṛtva being described concerns the fundamental power of consciousness, not the abilities of the biological organism.
blocks.directed: The kartṛtva being described concerns the fundamental power of consciousness, not the abilities of the biological organism.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja cites a passage from the Spandakārikā explaining a very subtle confusion.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja cites a passage from the Spandakārikā explaining a very subtle confusion.

blocks.text: When an activity-oriented effort disappears, an ignorant person may conclude:
blocks.directed: [short pause] When an activity-oriented effort disappears, an ignorant person may conclude:

blocks.text: But the disappearance of a particular mental operation is not the disappearance of the conscious reality through which it was experienced.
blocks.directed: But the disappearance of a particular mental operation is not the disappearance of the conscious reality through which it was experienced.

blocks.text: But the very possibility of experiencing their arising and cessation belongs to the conscious reality.
blocks.directed: But the very possibility of experiencing their arising and cessation belongs to the conscious reality.

blocks.text: And here’s the crucial metaphysical distinction.
blocks.directed: And here’s the crucial metaphysical distinction.

blocks.text: Consciousness is not simply another object within the sequence of objects.
blocks.directed: Consciousness is not simply another object within the sequence of objects.

blocks.text: If it were, we’d need another consciousness to know it.
blocks.directed: If it were, we’d need another consciousness to know it.

blocks.text: And then another to know that consciousness.
blocks.directed: And then another to know that consciousness.

blocks.text: And we’d have an absolutely catastrophic metaphysical staffing problem.
blocks.directed: And we’d have an absolutely catastrophic metaphysical staffing problem.

blocks.text: And nobody actually getting anything done.
blocks.directed: And nobody actually getting anything done.

blocks.text: Instead, Trika treats consciousness as svaprakāśa — self-luminous.
blocks.directed: Instead, Trika treats consciousness as svaprakāśa — self-luminous.

blocks.text: It is not known by a separate light.
blocks.directed: It is not known by a separate light.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja makes precisely this point when explaining why the supreme conscious knower doesn’t undergo the disappearance associated with its manifest objects.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja makes precisely this point when explaining why the supreme conscious knower doesn’t undergo the disappearance associated with its manifest objects.

blocks.text: He cites the Kālikākrama and Spandakārikā on the imperishable inner conscious nature beneath changing activity. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: He cites the Kālikākrama and Spandakārikā on the imperishable inner conscious nature beneath changing activity. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now this has a very interesting consequence.
blocks.directed: Now this has a very interesting consequence.

blocks.text: The aim of liberation cannot simply be to produce a particular object or mental state that will last forever.
blocks.directed: The aim of liberation cannot simply be to produce a particular object or mental state that will last forever.

blocks.text: Because the entire structure of objects belongs to changing manifestation.
blocks.directed: Because the entire structure of objects belongs to changing manifestation.

blocks.text: Instead, liberation concerns recognition of the conscious reality that is not fundamentally exhausted by those changes.
blocks.directed: Instead, liberation concerns recognition of the conscious reality that is not fundamentally exhausted by those changes.

blocks.text: And this is where the teaching becomes extraordinarily elegant.
blocks.directed: And this is where the teaching becomes extraordinarily elegant.

blocks.text: But none of these changes independently determines the fundamental nature of consciousness.
blocks.directed: But none of these changes independently determines the fundamental nature of consciousness.

blocks.text: And it brings us directly to the next sūtra.
blocks.directed: And it brings us directly to the next sūtra.

blocks.text: Because if pleasure and pain are changing contents of experience, what happens when the yogi stops identifying with them as the ultimate Self?
blocks.directed: Because if pleasure and pain are changing contents of experience, what happens when the yogi stops identifying with them as the ultimate Self?
